source.title: Understanding the training of infinitely deep and wide ResNets with conditional optimal transport
source.authors: Raphaël Barboni; Gabriel Peyré; François-Xavier Vialard

record.tranche_reason: The paper gives a theoretical gradient-flow convergence result for a mean-field, infinitely deep ResNet model and specifies sufficient initialization conditions. Its model and analysis differ from the finite benchmark experiments in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical convergence guarantees, not empirical benchmark training runs. Those theorems bear on V1 and V3 at the level of the paper's mean-field ResNet model. Cited results about other works are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves conditional convergence of gradient flow for an infinite-depth residual NODE. It does not test the versions' benchmark classification behavior, plain-versus-residual depth degradation, initialization-dependent signal propagation in plain networks, learning-rate stability, or normalization-dependent training speed. Its convergence theorems concern a related but different claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors establish a conditional optimal-transport formulation of residual NODE training and prove exponential risk decay and convergence to a global minimizer for suitable initializations with sufficiently small risk and sufficiently expressive features. They also give a lifting-and-output-scaling construction that enforces the convergence condition. Their results concern gradient flow; practical gradient descent is left open. The convergence analysis uses empirical data, excludes SHL ReLU under its smoothness assumptions, and does not establish escape from the kernel regime.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes conditional optimal transport gradient flow for an infinite-depth, arbitrary-width mean-field NODE/ResNet, with SHL residual examples and sufficient initialization conditions. It does not run the finite convolutional benchmark recipes described in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Convergence depends on initialization, kernel conditioning, initial risk, feature count, and—in the lifting result—the loss scale α.

fits_no_version.finding: For smooth SHL residual NODEs, positive initial kernel conditioning and sufficiently small initial risk imply exponential risk decay and parameter convergence; the rate bound is proportional to λ0/N.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Infinite-depth residual NODEs admit conditional global convergence guarantees under local kernel-conditioning and initial-risk assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: Embedding inputs into a larger space and using a sufficiently large output scale guarantees convergence from identity initialization when the feature kernel is positive definite.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lifting inputs and scaling the output can enforce sufficient conditions for gradient-flow convergence in smooth residual NODEs.

record.peer_reviewed: Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics
record.problems: The findings are theoretical sufficient-condition results rather than benchmark experiments. The authors identify gradient flow as an idealization of gradient descent, note that their convergence analysis assumes an empirical data distribution and has a P-Ł constant scaling as N⁻¹, and cannot use the analysis for SHL ReLU under its differentiability assumptions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying study results on the versions were reported. Statements about prior work in the introduction and related work were excluded because they are citations, not this study's own results.

untested.parts: Finite convolutional networks trained from random initialization with SGD or Adam on CIFAR-10/100; training classification error, label corruption, model-size effects, early stopping and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization, frequencies of spurious minima, and the effect of adding one or two student neurons.
Training-error degradation with increasing plain-network depth, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified plain-tanh and normalization-free residual training results.
Activation-matched signal and gradient preservation in plain networks, training-speed or trainable-depth comparisons, and orthogonal-versus-Gaussian initialization.
Discrete learning rates, stability thresholds, loss transients, curvature evolution, edge-of-stability behavior and divergence.
Accuracy gains and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, and comparative speed and stability of Fixup training.

record.verdict_notes: A sufficient condition is not evidence that training fails outside that condition. Consequently, the low-risk, lifting and scaling assumptions do not justify the record's limits_scope labels. References to Fixup and shortcut benefits do not supply this study's own comparative results on V3 or V6.

versions.untested_parts: No finite convolutional networks, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 benchmark experiments, SGD or Adam runs, or corrupted/random-label tests. The analysis concerns gradient flow for a mean-field NODE/ResNet model and convergence to a global minimizer under sufficient conditions.

No empirical comparison of plain and shortcut networks at increasing depth. The model is a residual NODE, and the paper's convergence condition uses a specified initialization; it does not compare against a plain network.

rows.subject: mean-field NODE model with SHL residuals
rows.size_stated: arbitrary width; sufficiently (but possibly finitely) many features
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical gradient flow from an initialization satisfying the stated kernel-conditioning and low-initial-risk conditions.
rows.measure: training risk and convergence of parameters to a global minimizer
rows.value: Theorem 4.2: L(μt) ≤ L(μ0) exp(−Cλ0t/N), and μt converges to μ∞ as t→∞.
rows.note: This is a sufficient-condition theorem, not an empirical result. The model is a mean-field residual NODE; the conclusion is convergence to a global minimizer, not a reported classification-error measurement.
rows.check: Theorem 4.2 establishes conditional risk convergence for smooth SHL residual NODEs, not V1's convolutional classification error or V3's depth degradation and shortcut comparison. The recorded exponential bound correctly includes division by N.

rows.subject: mean-field ResNet model
rows.size_stated: sufficiently large but finite number of features
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical gradient flow from an initialization with sufficiently low risk and satisfying a local Polyak–Łojasiewicz condition.

conditions.value: sufficiently low risk and local P-Ł property
mean-field ResNet of infinite depth and arbitrary width

rows.measure: risk convergence and convergence to a global minimizer
rows.value: Theorem 4.1: L(μt) ≤ e−mt L(μ0); μT exists and d(μT, μ0) ≤ R. The paper's contribution summary states convergence to a global minimizer for sufficiently large but finite features and sufficiently low initial risk.
rows.note: General theorem conditional on a local P-Ł property; the paper does not assert this condition for arbitrary initializations.
rows.check: Theorem 4.1 is explicitly attributed to SMP23 and should not be a separate row of this study's own findings. It gives a general local P-Ł implication, conditional on an existing curve; the study's architecture-specific convergence result is already R1. Neither establishes V1 or V3.

rows.subject: mean-field NODE model with SHL residuals
rows.size_stated: arbitrary width; feature count may be finite and sufficiently large
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical gradient flow from a FixUp-style identity initialization, with convergence condition enforced by lifting inputs and scaling the loss.

conditions.value: embed inputs in higher-dimensional space and use rescaled loss Lα

rows.measure: convergence to a global minimizer of Lα
rows.value: Proposition 4.5: for α > α0, the gradient flow initialized at μ0 converges to a global minimizer of Lα.
rows.note: The guaranteed result is for the modified, lifted and rescaled problem, not an unmodified benchmark classification recipe.
rows.check: Proposition 4.5 concerns a lifted NODE with a scaled output projection and squared loss, ℓα(z,y)=½‖αBz−y‖². Calling this merely loss scaling obscures the modification. It establishes neither benchmark classification performance nor a depth or normalization comparison.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.reason: The paper proves convergence of gradient-flow risk to zero and convergence to a global minimizer under these conditions (R1, R2). This supports only the conditional theoretical case, not the benchmark and optimizer settings in V1.
